objective.statement: Fix the Home View bordered div so its border is blue and dashed instead of green.

complexity.rationale: Two Tailwind class changes on one element in HomeView.tsx plus the one test that asserts the old colour; no new state, dependency or contract.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The bordered div on the Home View renders a blue border (border-blue-500) instead of green.
The bordered div renders a dashed border style (border-dashed).
The div no longer carries border-green-500 or border-red-500, and its other behaviour (200px size, centred 8px text, 2px width, rounded corners, text) is unchanged.

in.statement: src/views/home/HomeView.tsx: change the bordered div's colour class from border-green-500 to border-blue-500 and add border-dashed.
src/views/home/HomeView.component.test.tsx: replace the green-border assertion with blue and dashed assertions.

out.statement: Renaming the redBorderedSquare test id, the aria-label "Red bordered square", or the test titles that mention red; any other element's border; theme tokens; new dependencies or config.

observations.statement: Render HomeView: the div with data-id home-view-red-bordered-square has className border-2 border-green-500 and no border-dashed, so it shows a solid green border.

The green colour was introduced deliberately by the earlier change-home-view-border-to-green workflow; this card supersedes it. HomeView.component.test.tsx 'should render a green border instead of a red one' asserts the old class and must be replaced, not left failing.

"Blue" means the Tailwind palette blue-500, the same shade step as the previous green-500, and "dashed" means the border-dashed utility with the existing 2px width. Raw palette classes are already used on this element rather than theme tokens.
The 'green bordered div' is the single bordered div in HomeView; the legacy red-bordered naming of its test id and aria-label is left alone to keep the fix minimal.

provenance.source: Card: Bug Fix - Wrong border colour. The green bordered div should be blue and dashed.
Card says blue without a shade; conservative choice is Tailwind blue-500, matching the green-500 it replaces.
Card does not ask to rename the red-bordered test id or aria-label; conservative choice is to leave them untouched.
Existing behaviour of the div (size, centring, text size, text) must stay as covered by existing tests; the stale green assertion is replaced.

capabilityOwners.rationale: The border is static render output on HomeView; no state is involved.
Border styling is not client state.

unit.rationale: No logic or pure function changes; the fix is a className change.

component.rationale: The rendered HomeView element must carry the blue and dashed classes and not the green one.

integration.rationale: No cross-module behaviour changes; the full npm test suite still runs as regression verification (App.component.test.tsx renders HomeView).

e2e.rationale: Pure styling of an already component-tested element; no routed flow changes.

increments.behavior: The Home View bordered div renders border-blue-500 and border-dashed instead of border-green-500.
increments.doneWhen: The component tests for blue and dashed pass, the stale green assertion is gone, the full suite is green, and tsc and eslint are clean.

tests.description: HomeView bordered div has class border-blue-500 and carries neither border-green-500 nor border-red-500.
HomeView bordered div has class border-dashed.

expectedRedEvidence.expectedFailure: expect(className).toContain('border-blue-500') fails because the div still has border-green-500.
expect(className).toContain('border-dashed') fails because the div has no dashed utility.

verification.requirement: HomeView component tests for blue and dashed pass and the other HomeView tests still pass.
Full suite (npm run test), tsc build and eslint pass with no regression in App tests.
